name: Pallof Press
description: The Pallof press is an anti-rotation core stability exercise using a cable or resistance band. The load is set at a fixed angle perpendicular to the body and the lifter presses it out and back while resisting the rotational pull. It trains the core musculature to stabilize the spine against rotation, which is fundamental for athletic performance and spinal health.

execution.starting_position: Stand (or kneel) sideways to a cable machine at mid-torso height. Hold the handle with both hands against the chest. Stand far enough that the cable is taut and pulling the hands toward the machine.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the pulley to chest height. Attach a single handle. The load should be moderate — this is a stability, not strength, exercise.
steps: Press the cable handle straight out in front of the chest, extending the arms fully.
Hold the extended position for 2–3 seconds while resisting the rotational pull of the cable.
Return the handle back to the chest under control.
Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you press out. Breathe normally while holding.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso toward the cable — the core must resist this
Using too much weight — the goal is stability, not strength
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the press. Hold for the prescribed duration before returning.
coaching_cues: Do not let the cable twist your body — stay square to the wall in front of you
Brace the core before pressing — think about being a stone wall
